newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Report urges A$1 billion government incentive fund.
newsitem.headline: Report urges A$1 billion government incentive fund.

text.p: An official report to the Australian industry minister John Moore recommended on Wednesday that the government establish a A$1 billion fund to provide incentives for new investment.

A report entitled "Going for Growth", written by TNT Asia/Pacific chief executive David Mortimer, also advised the government to target a doubling of Australia's per capita income growth rate from the current 1.7 percent to an average 3.4 percent over the next 10 years.

Mortimer told a news conference the report recommended a reshuffling of current spending on industry programmes into five new areas with forecast spending over the five years from 1998/99 to 2002/03 of A$20.75 billion.
Mortimer said this represented net extra spending of about A$900 million over the five years forecast.
He also said the report recommended a revamp of foreign investment rules, limiting the current Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) to making decisions on foreign ownership of real estate only.
Industry Minister John Moore told a news conference he welcomed the report's recommendations and the government would give its response within a short period.
"I think it could be a cornerstone of the Australian economy between now and the APEC (Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation) deadline in 2010," Moore said.
Australia has agreed as one of APEC's industrialised nations to remove all its trade barriers by 2010, while APEC's developing nations have agreed to remove their barriers by 2020.

Mortimer said the A$1 billion investment incentive fund, to be called Invest Australia, would concentrate on analysing new investment projects, helping them clear bureaucratic hurdles and providing incentives for the new investment.
"The reality is that in our near region there are a lot of countries providing incentives to invest," he said.
He added that Australia must strive to try and recreate the conditions that has seen many East Asian economies achieve annual per capita growth of 5.4 percent over the last 10 years.
Any project approved by Invest Australia would have to clearly demonstrate spill over benefits in excess of the costs of any incentives granted.
The report also recommends the establishment of a single research and development incentive scheme open to all businesses.
The R&D tax concession would be set at 100 percent compared with the existing 125 percent rebate for certain types of R&D.
